applicant_utility.summary: The EAN Clinical Fellowship pays EUR 425 per week for a clinical observership of 6 to 12 weeks at an approved EAN hosting department, outside your own country, at a minimum of 5 days a week, and reimburses up to EUR 300 of travel once the fellowship ends. Applications for 2027 are open until 31 October 2026, but you cannot apply at all unless a named hosting supervisor has already accepted you and signed the acceptance form. Three separate scores decide the outcome - the application, the CV and the overall impression - so the case you make for why that specific department and that specific length of stay matters more than your publication record.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Residents and early-career neurologists with at least two years of clinical training who need to see a specific technique or a specific service model running at another European department and to bring it back home. Applicants who already know which department, which supervisor and which length of stay they want, and have written to that department, are the realistic candidates; the programme is not a general travel grant.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your RRFS or Full EAN membership is active; if applying for membership, submit at least 3 weeks before the deadline because approval can take 10 working days
Confirm you have at least 2 years of clinical (residency) training in neurology and a hospital declaration to prove it
Choose an approved hosting department from the EAN list and secure an acceptance form with a supervisor who will have at least weekly direct contact
Agree the length of the stay - between 6 and 12 weeks at 5 days per week
Write the explanation of why and how the fellowship in that particular department is relevant and why that length of stay
Obtain two letters of recommendation from two individual neurologists
Log into MyEAN to access the form
common_rejection_risks: Applying without a signed acceptance form from an approved hosting department
Inactive or pending EAN membership at the point of application, which blocks access to the form entirely
Weak explanation of why this particular hosting department and why this particular length of stay
A stay under 6 weeks or over 12 weeks, or fewer than 5 days per week
Two recommendation letters from the same neurologist, or from someone who is not a neurologist
No supervisor available for at least weekly direct contact during the fellowship
Destroying the original documents before the outcome is notified, since fresh copies may be requested
For the Ukraine and low and lower-middle income country routes, overlooking the eligibility category that applies
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: With EUR 425 a week and up to EUR 300 of travel reimbursed after the stay, you fund your own flights up front, plus the Students Union or registration fees, local transport, food and insurance for a stay of 6 to 12 weeks in another country. Travel is reimbursed only at the end, so the flight money must be available in advance.
applicant_utility.document_audit: Four files are needed: the application form, the host acceptance form, the training evidence with the hospital declaration, and two separate neurologist reference letters. Check that the acceptance form names the supervisor contact and confirms weekly direct contact, and that the hospital declaration states the length of training explicitly.

applicant_utility.summary: The EAN Research Fellowship pays EUR 2,000 a month for a research spell at a European academic neurology department outside your own country, with up to EUR 500 of travel reimbursed after the close-out paperwork. The 2027 window closed on 31 August 2026 and notifications go out by the end of November 2026, so the next realistic opening is mid-2027. Scoring is granular - four marks split across originality, feasibility, usefulness for your career and methods, two for you, two for the proposed host plus the supervisor, and one overall impression - so the host department and the named mentor count as heavily as your own CV.
applicant_utility.best_fit: RRFS members and early-career Full members in EAN Full Institutional Member countries who already have a specific project, a specific host department and a specific mentor abroad, and who can show the training will bring something back to their home department that is not available there. Residents with more than two years of neurology training suit the RRFS route, while Full members up to five years past their latest degree also qualify.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your RRFS or Full EAN membership is active, joining at least 3 weeks before the deadline because approval can take 10 working days
Confirm you meet the category: RRFS member with more than 2 years of residency training, or Full member no more than 5 years past your latest neurology degree
Secure a letter of acceptance from the chair of the host institution, with a short CV and short bibliography of the proposed mentor
Obtain the recommendation form from the chair of your home department
Obtain a recommendation letter from another neurologist
Draft the project description with background, aims, methods, timetable and references
Complete the EAN CV form with your list of publications
Prepare the English document confirming your neurology training and its duration
Submit everything via the EAN online application form - e-mailed or hand-written applications are not considered
common_rejection_risks: Inactive or pending EAN membership, which makes you ineligible to apply
A host department inside your own country of residence
No named host mentor with a CV and bibliography attached to the acceptance letter
A project that does not show a clear gain for the home department beyond what is available locally
Weak feasibility or methods, which carry extra weight in the nine-part score
Applying by e-mail instead of through the online form
Discarding original documents before the outcome, since fresh copies may be requested
Assuming previous EAN awardee status improves your chances - it does not
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: With EUR 2,000 a month and up to EUR 500 of travel reimbursed only after the evaluation forms from both fellow and mentor and your final report are submitted, you fund your own relocation, flights up front, insurance, visa and registration costs, plus any residence gap before the fellowship formally starts.
applicant_utility.document_audit: Six items, all in English where specified. The host acceptance letter must include the mentor's short CV and bibliography - a plain invitation letter is not enough. The home department recommendation must come from the chair, not from your line supervisor.
